label: Aquinas on lordship and the naming bridges
summary: I q.13 a.7 grounds real divine lordship in real creaturely subjection and places temporality on the creature's side. I q.13 a.11 co. connects Qui est with divine esse as identical with essence. Ad 1 distinguishes how the name is imposed and signifies from what the name is imposed to signify: Deus is more proper on the latter criterion as a name of the divine nature. The article neither identifies arbitrary stage-one God parameters with the full classical profile nor quantifies over who is called God by a speech community. Its description of the name does not show that satisfaction of the full nominal description determines community usage.
blocker: For lordship, show why the route's generic causation warrants real subjection. For the naming routes prove identification of the same stage-one witness with the classical profile or defend the independent rule governing community usage.
